statement_record.book: Two contravariant functors S-bar : A -> X and T-bar : X -> A are adjoint on the right when there is a bijection A(a, T-bar x) ≅ X(x, S-bar a) natural in a and x; rewriting with the covariant S : A^op -> X, T : X^op -> A this says exactly that S^op is left adjoint to T (equivalently T^op left adjoint to S); adjointness on the right is not in general equivalent to adjointness on the left for such a pair.
statement_record.intree: No in-tree definition names the notion. The equivalent covariant unfolding the book itself gives is expressible verbatim with existing machinery: the Adjunction class applied to S^op ⊣ T, the strictly involutive opposite (C^op^op = C), and Opposite_Adjunction : F ⊣ U → U^op ⊣ F^op with Opposite_Adjunction_invol providing the T^op ⊣ S ↔ S^op ⊣ T transposition.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the reduction target (adjunctions between opposite categories, with the op-involution and the flip lemma) is fully present, but the notion 'adjoint on the right' itself — the symmetric two-contravariant-functor packaging, its name, the natural bijection stated in that form, and Mac Lane's warning that right-adjointness and left-adjointness of such a pair differ — is never defined, stated, or instantiated.
